interpretations.rationale: Current account of both mechanisms this question turned up in the actor layer's `append_notify` completion path, with their conditions as the retained runs support them. First, the resolution arms: `drain_notifiers` answers `Ok(assigned_idx)` as soon as the local decided index reaches the index recorded at assignment, before it evaluates the ballot-change arm and without comparing the caller's entry with what occupies that index, and it runs only from the actor's tick branch. A write whose entry was accepted only by the leader it was assigned to, then dropped by a leader change, therefore resolves `Ok` with an index that holds a different entry; the same lost-entry state resolves the documented `Superseded` instead when a tick falls between the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance, and the two arms are separated by the tick period against the re-synchronisation round trip: with a ~2 ms round trip the sweep held at 2 and 4 ms ticks and violated at 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms, and the crate's own default tick period is 10 ms. Second, the assignment mapping: deferred writes are tracked as one placeholder per buffered entry, one placeholder is consumed per unit of accepted-index advance, and a placeholder is discarded while still consuming its advance when its buffered ballot no longer matches the promise; a re-synchronisation that truncates entries whose placeholders are still queued therefore shifts the index later reported to a caller, and the retained runs show the shift (index 4 while entry 33 sits at 2, or 3 while it sits at 1, with the returned index holding entry 35) in the configurations where the origin's two entries were still in its batch at the truncation, and no shift where the flush deadline had already removed them (a two-tick deadline at 1000 or 100 ms) or where it fired before the re-synchronisation (100 and 250 ms ticks with the default hundred-tick deadline). Both mechanisms end in the same caller-visible shape - a success resolution naming an index that does not hold the caller's entry - and the repository's own caller of this API treats that resolution as synchronous durability confirmation of the entry at that index, announcing it without re-reading the log, while the existing runtime test only asserts a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix. A value check in `drain_notifiers` would mask both symptoms without fixing either cause: the arm order and the placeholder accounting are independent defects.
counterevidence: The success resolution is documented only as the assigned log index being decided, with the advice to re-read the returned index only for `Superseded`; read that way `Ok(idx)` claims nothing about the value at `idx`, so a caller that verifies the entry itself is not misled. That weakens the caller-facing consequence but not the schedule dependence of the first mechanism nor the mis-assignment of the second.

A new leader must adopt any value a majority-overlapping write quorum already accepted, so an entry that reached a write quorum cannot be replaced; both mechanisms therefore need the assignment to be local-only or the entries to be discarded, which the receipts support (origin decided index 0 in the violating runs, the new leader's decided values excluding the origin's entries).

No retained run exhibits the two mechanisms together in one call, nor a re-synchronisation that both completes and carries decided progress while the origin's entries are discarded, so the intermediate steps of the second mechanism remain unobserved even though its endpoints are complete and reproduced.

The placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so its accounting is the explanation the endpoints imply rather than a direct measurement; the flush-deferral and accept-sync rules behind the condition are source-derived and consistent with the phase fields of the runs.
limitations: Six retained configurations, all with batch_size 3 at the origin, a three-node cluster, majority quorum, a leader origin and an in-process in-memory transport; follower origins, other batch sizes, flexible quorums and crash recovery are unmeasured.

interpretations.rationale: Current account of both mechanisms this question turned up in the actor layer's `append_notify` completion path, with their conditions as the retained runs support them. First, the resolution arms: `drain_notifiers` answers `Ok(assigned_idx)` as soon as the local decided index reaches the index recorded at assignment, before it evaluates the ballot-change arm and without comparing the caller's entry with what occupies that index, and it runs only from the actor's tick branch. A write whose entry was accepted only by the leader it was assigned to, then dropped by a leader change, therefore resolves `Ok` with an index that holds a different entry; the same lost-entry state resolves the documented `Superseded` instead when a tick falls between the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance, and the two arms are separated by the tick period against the re-synchronisation round trip: with a ~2 ms round trip the sweep held at 2 and 4 ms ticks and violated at 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms, and the crate's own default tick period is 10 ms. Second, the assignment mapping: deferred writes are tracked as one placeholder per buffered entry, one placeholder is consumed per unit of accepted-index advance, and a placeholder is discarded while still consuming its advance when its buffered ballot no longer matches the promise; a re-synchronisation that truncates entries whose placeholders are still queued therefore shifts the index later reported to a caller, and the retained runs show the shift (index 4 while entry 33 sits at 2, or 3 while it sits at 1, with the returned index holding entry 35) in the configurations where the origin's two entries were still in its batch at the truncation, and no shift where the flush deadline had already removed them (a two-tick deadline at 1000 or 100 ms) or where it fired before the re-synchronisation (100 and 250 ms ticks with the default hundred-tick deadline). Both mechanisms end in the same caller-visible shape - a success resolution naming an index that does not hold the caller's entry - and the repository's own caller of this API treats that resolution as synchronous durability confirmation of the entry at that index, announcing it without re-reading the log, while the existing runtime test only asserts a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix. A value check in `drain_notifiers` would mask both symptoms without fixing either cause: the arm order and the placeholder accounting are independent defects.
counterevidence: The success resolution is documented only as the assigned log index being decided, with the advice to re-read the returned index only for `Superseded`; read that way `Ok(idx)` claims nothing about the value at `idx`, so a caller that verifies the entry itself is not misled. That weakens the caller-facing consequence but not the schedule dependence of the first mechanism nor the mis-assignment of the second.

A new leader must adopt any value a majority-overlapping write quorum already accepted, so an entry that reached a write quorum cannot be replaced; both mechanisms therefore need the assignment to be local-only or the entries to be discarded, which the receipts support (origin decided index 0 in the violating runs, the new leader's decided values excluding the origin's entries).

No retained run exhibits the two mechanisms together in one call, nor a re-synchronisation that both completes and carries decided progress while the origin's entries are discarded, so the intermediate steps of the second mechanism remain unobserved even though its endpoints are complete and reproduced.
